page.layout: Running head at top centre; page number top right; emblem title as a centred heading in two lines with the number XXXX at the right; a woodcut illustration in the middle of the page; a verse poem of six lines below the woodcut, with an initial V; no notes in the margins; no catchword or signature.

main_text.l: [Woodcut illustration: a man fleeing across water, a rocky landscape, and a figure at a burning pyre on the right.]
VIdi ego carnificis metuentem verbera savi,
Qui medias sese Ligeris proiecit in undas,
Et quanuis sudore madens, expérsque natandi
Fluminis evasit pede calcans ima profundi,
Quem mox non ina poenas pro cede luentem
Hac age dispicito recta qui tramite vita
Deserto, magis atque magis periturus oberras:
Nam quo tardior est, gravior fit numinis ira.

page.notes: The woodcut is described above and not transcribed. The verse has several evident printing irregularities (long s and f forms, "savi" for "saevi", "Ligeris", "ina" for "una", "cede" for "caede", "oberras"); the letters were copied as printed where legible, with [?] omitted because the printed text itself is clear, but the initial "V" of the verse is a woodcut-style letter and the word "expérsque" may be misread. Verse lines were kept as printed as separate lines in one paragraph.
